subject: general
question: Which of the following is the autobiography of the first female judge of India, Anna Chandy?
solution:
The correct answer is **__Atmakatha__.**

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**Atmakatha

__
 
• **Justice Anna Chandy** was** India’s first female judge** and **the first woman in the country to become a High court judge.**
 
• She has been described as a **‘first-generation feminist’.**
 
• She contested from **Shree Mulam Popular Assembly** and was elected for the term 1932-34.
 
• She became **the first woman judge** in **the Indian district court in 1937.**
 
• She was **the 2nd woman in the world who reached the high court judgeship in 1959. **
 
• In 1971 the Malayala Manorama serialized her autobiography which was subsequently published in Thrissur by Carmel Books in 1973 under the title Atmakatha. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** __**Atmavrittanta**__

__
 
• **Atmavrittanta,** formally published as **Manilal Nabhubhai Dwivedinu Atmavrittanta,** is an autobiography written by **Gujarati writer Manilal Nabhubhai Dwivedi.**
 
• **At the age of 28**,** Manilal decided to write his autobiography** and maintain a diary of important events until the end of his life.
 
• Manilal handed over the manuscript of his autobiography to his trusted friend** Anandshankar Dhruv **before his death in **1898**.

**Majya Jalmachi Chittarkatha**__

__
 
• **Maya Jalmachi Chittarkatha** is an **autobiography of Shantabai Kamble** published in **1983.**
 
• This is considered the **first autobiographical narrative** by a **Dalit woman writer.**
 
• This book shows the life of an Indian woman who was from the lower class of the caste.

**Ente Katha**__

 
• **Ente Kadha (My Story) **is an **autobiography written by Kamala Surayya (Madhavikutty)** in the year** 1973.**
 
• She was motivated to write this as she became ill and thought will not survive.
 
• The book was** controversial and outspoken** and had her critics gunning her after it was published in **1973**.
